points.why: It places (a) as a parameter that leaves the enforcement loop unchanged and fades like the blitzes, (b) as a rule locking safe design into repaving, and (c) as a goal change redefining a good project.
It rates power and reach separately: (c) is highest but hardest and slow to show up, (b) acts only at the repaving rate, and (a) is weak and will fade.
It keeps blitzes as a cheap stopgap and labels (b) a bridge to (c), but drops fines outright, though for stated deterrence reasons rather than on principle.
It gives a clear sequence, but there is no pilot corridor or modeling test and no open trade-off such as longer car trips.

pitfalls.why: It pairs (c) with (b) as an interim rule rather than choosing (c) alone.
It explicitly says blitzes are not a strategy.
